title: Leading With Nexus
description: For managers and above: how to run a team and a business on Nexus. The leader's day, approvals and the recommendation, shifts and the planner, Time Sheet review, the scorecard, the ticket desk, people from hiring to exits, training the team and keeping courses current, communicating, the money and property views, and access, settings and the record. Course 10 of the Academy.
overview: The leader's day: decisions, the team's view, the Team widgets
Approvals: every kind, the recommendation, punch fixes, phones and delegates
Shifts and the planner: rules that warn, Share and Confirm, the day's notices
Time Sheet review: the attention strip, approve or send back, only the employee signs
The ticket desk as a leader: queues, clocks, Preventive, what stays invisible
People: hiring, onboarding, probation, performance, exits
Training your team and keeping courses current
Communicating: announcements, Teams, Notes and Boards
Money and property views; access, settings and the record
teaches: Dashboard, Approvals, Team, Shift Planner, Time Sheet, Time Off, Workforce Analytics, Tickets, People, Hiring, Knowledge Base, Training, Announcements, Notes, Settings, Asset Management, Accounting

questions.q: What are the two things a leader looks at every morning?
options: Who is here, and what is waiting on you
questions.explanation: Team Attendance and Time Exceptions; the Approvals tab and the bell.

questions.q: An approval given in the hallway is:
options: Not an approval until it is in Nexus; the person is not told and no record stands
questions.explanation: Decide in Nexus, every time.

questions.q: A time off request reads Check First. That means:
options: Nexus found a reason to look: coverage, notice, balance or the calendar; the decision is still yours
questions.explanation: Nothing is approved or rejected by code.

questions.q: A punch fix asks for a 6:30 PM clock-out with the reason 'stayed late' and nothing else. What do you do?
options: Send it back asking what kept them, such as a ticket number or their End of Day message
questions.explanation: A punch fix changes a pay record; the standard is evidence.

questions.q: The schedule rules in the Shift Planner:
options: Block a share that breaks them
Warn, never block; sharing past a warning needs a reason kept on the change log
questions.explanation: The reason is never shown to staff.

questions.q: Confirm on a shared schedule means:
options: The person agrees to every shift forever
The person has seen it; a problem is a conversation or a shift request
questions.explanation: The planner shows who has not confirmed; a nudge follows.

questions.q: A Time Sheet is signed by:
options: The employee only; the manager's approval is a review
questions.explanation: The PDF carries the approval log with the manager's name.

questions.q: Before approving a Time Sheet, decide the change requests first because:
options: An approved request changes the hours
questions.explanation: Then read the attention strip and the days.

lessons.checkpoint: Checkpoint: The Desk, People and Training

questions.q: Expected hours for a part-timer with no shared shift are:
questions.explanation: Share their shifts, or accept that the scorecard cannot score them.

questions.q: Which queue is worked first, every hour at the desk?
questions.explanation: The requester spoke last, or nobody has replied yet.

questions.q: A leader with the Tickets grant asks to see Ask HR tickets. The right answer is:
options: No; confidential HR tickets are visible to HR's audience only, by design
questions.explanation: The private channel for pay and policy questions without the manager in the thread.

questions.q: Who finalizes a probation decision?
options: HR; the manager's Confirm, Extend or End is a recommendation
questions.explanation: End opens the Offboard flow, never a second path.

questions.q: Which signs first on an HR document?
options: The employee, always; the company countersigns after
questions.explanation: No pre-signed or countersigned document is ever sent out.

questions.q: A training escalation reaching you means:
options: A course is still not done after its due date; a nudge to a conversation about what is in the way
questions.explanation: Usually time on the schedule or a locked quiz.

questions.q: A course flagged 'Nexus changed since this course was reviewed' asks the owner to:
options: Read the lessons that teach the changed module, then publish edits or Mark Reviewed
questions.explanation: Courses follow the product.

questions.q: Where do conversations happen at Greens?
options: On Microsoft Teams; decisions in Nexus
questions.explanation: Nexus has no chat of its own, on purpose.

questions.q: The Team widgets on the Dashboard are found under:
options: Team, in Add Widget, for managers and above
questions.explanation: Team Attendance, Team Approvals, Pending Approvals, Who Has What, Team Time, Ticket Queue, Time Exceptions, Out Today, Pending Purchases, My Team.

questions.q: A leader's Dashboard should be:
options: A control room built from the Team widgets, saved as the default
questions.explanation: Build it once.

questions.q: Which of these gains come with leading a team in Nexus? Pick all that apply.
options: Decisions in Approvals and the bell
The team's view in Team > Shifts and the widgets
questions.explanation: Managers never see pay.

questions.q: Delegate My Approvals is set:
options: Before you are away, for the days you name
questions.explanation: A team whose leader is away with no delegate has a week nobody can answer.

questions.q: On a phone, Approvals shows:
options: One card at a time with two decisions; no bulk approve
questions.explanation: Each decision is read before it is made.

questions.q: A no with no reason written is:
options: A decision that will not stand and a person who cannot ask for different days
questions.explanation: Say why.

questions.q: Which approval kinds come to a site leader? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: Pay is HR's.

questions.q: Fill Automatically:
options: Lays each person's usual hours onto the week, skipping holidays and approved time off, and says how many days it skipped
questions.explanation: Copy Week does the same for a past week.

questions.q: The no-show rollup is:
options: One bell per team and day, resolved in place as people arrive
questions.explanation: Call the person.

questions.q: Shift swaps and open shifts are:
options: Off by default, switched on per company in Settings > Shifts & Scheduling
questions.explanation: The teammate accepts first; then the manager.

questions.q: Managers see labor cost in the planner.
questions.explanation: The planner shows hours; the labor budget is HR and above.

questions.q: Weather calls apply to:
options: People in departments with Weather Calls on, Construction by default
questions.explanation: A storage team's week is not cancelled by weather.

questions.q: The attention strip on a Time Sheet lists:
options: What to look at before approving: missing punches, location words, break reports, empty scheduled days
questions.explanation: Read it first.

questions.q: A missed-break report from an hourly California employee means:
options: Add the premium pay; the card goes back for signature
questions.explanation: Never ask anyone to sign a statement that is not true.

questions.q: Which reopens an approved Time Sheet? Pick all that apply.
options: The employee declining in Nexus Sign with a reason
questions.explanation: The envelope is voided and the period reopens to the manager.

questions.q: A Time Sheet nobody can sign (the person left) is finalized by:
questions.explanation: Never by hiding the signature step.

questions.q: Review every Time Sheet:
options: The day after the period ends
questions.explanation: Payroll waits with you.

questions.q: The Workforce Scorecard measures:
options: Punched hours against expected hours, weekly
questions.explanation: Attendance against expectation, not pay.

questions.q: A Viewer of the Workforce Scorecard sees:
questions.explanation: Editor the line; Full the company.

questions.q: A whole day missing against a shared shift is usually:
options: A no-show, a forgotten punch, or a shift that should have been changed
questions.explanation: Check the no-show rollup and the person's messages.

questions.q: The rule behind the analytics is:
options: The Workforce Analytics Policy under Settings, per company
questions.explanation: Read it before you act on a number.

questions.q: Which queues stand as tabs on the desk?
options: Needs Reply, Unassigned, Mine, All Open
questions.explanation: The rest sit in Other Queues.

questions.q: The Next Clock is red when:
questions.explanation: The one SLA wording on the list.

questions.q: Tickets should be assigned to:
options: A person, the day they arrive
questions.explanation: A ticket with a name has a clock that someone feels.

questions.q: The Preventive queue's count is:
options: The overdue ones, in red when any
questions.explanation: Zero overdue means the building is being kept.

questions.q: An Administrator sees tickets from:
options: Every company; the pickers stay walled
questions.explanation: The one carve-out in the walls.

questions.q: A team member wants their job title corrected. They should:
options: Ask their manager to change it
questions.explanation: The record itself is HR's; Ask HR is the confidential channel.

questions.q: My Numbers on the Performance tab are:
options: Worked out by Nexus from what it already records; never time off, sick days, pay or HR requests
questions.explanation: Seen by the person, their managers and HR.

questions.q: An exit starts:
options: In the Offboard flow in People > Exits, by HR or from a probation End
questions.explanation: Nexus then clears shifts, access, equipment and the unsigned Time Sheet in order.

questions.q: Contractors and guests are tracked for probation.
questions.explanation: Only new employees, by start date.

questions.q: A role path is:
options: A learning path of kind role whose audience is job titles
questions.explanation: Department training targets departments the same way.

questions.q: A course can reach a person by which ways? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: Four ways.

questions.q: Before unlocking a locked quiz:
options: Talk with the person about what to reread; the report shows their misses
questions.explanation: The hardest questions are the author's next edit too.

questions.q: In-person sign-off is given:
options: Only for work the trainer or manager saw
questions.explanation: Completed In Person.

questions.q: The Refresher is:
options: Three questions a day from the courses a person passed, theirs alone
questions.explanation: What you will notice is a team that remembers.

questions.q: Learn This Screen in the Help panel offers:
options: The course and lessons that teach the current screen
questions.explanation: The same teaches tag powers the review flag.

questions.q: Announcements show on a Dashboard through:
options: The Announcements widget, which must be added
questions.explanation: Tell every new team member to add it.

questions.q: Only who posts announcements?
options: Administrators; a leader asks or drafts for them
questions.explanation: Audience, notify mode, Acknowledge.

questions.q: A Board is:
options: A drawing in Notes: a lot layout, a marked-up photo, a plan
questions.explanation: Mark Up any photo or PDF and attach it back to its ticket.

questions.q: A problem written in a note:
options: Is a problem nobody else will read; it goes in a ticket or a form
questions.explanation: A note is never a report.

questions.q: With one entity, Accounting shows a site leader:
options: Their site's statements and reports with the drill-down
questions.explanation: The Dashboard tabs are consolidated.

questions.q: Who sees a construction job's dollars?
options: People with the cost view, the Accounting grant and entity access together
questions.explanation: Contract and change-order dollars follow the permission everywhere.

questions.q: Before approving a purchase request, check:
options: Item Management for an existing one, the justification and the limits
questions.explanation: The company may already own it.

questions.q: Company on an asset is:
options: A field; administrators see every company's assets, only assigning a company is limited

questions.q: An Administrator can see another company's people if asked nicely.
questions.explanation: An Administrator is always walled; only a Super Administrator or a global group crosses.

questions.q: A tier is:
options: How much you may approve and how far your view reaches
questions.explanation: A grant is a module opened at a level.

questions.q: A team member cannot see the ticket desk. The right fix is:
options: Ask the administrator to add them to the Access Group, or raise a ticket for access
questions.explanation: A shared sign-in makes every punch and approval someone else's.

questions.q: Every setting has:
options: One scope: the organization, one company, or a default a company may override
questions.explanation: Administrators change; leaders ask.

questions.q: The record Nexus keeps of a leader's decisions:
options: Is what lets a decision stand a year later and protects the leader who decides in Nexus
questions.explanation: Decide in Nexus, with the reason.

questions.q: Under a person's name the screen shows:
options: Their job title; the tier is a small mark beside the name
questions.explanation: A filled shield, an outline shield, a people glyph.

questions.q: Which are the five Super Administrators set in 11/2026?
questions.explanation: Changed in Settings, never in code.

questions.q: Needs Reply is decided by:
questions.explanation: The requester spoke last, or nobody has replied yet.

questions.q: The attention strip belongs to:
questions.explanation: What to look at before approving.

questions.q: Ask HR is:
options: The confidential desk for pay and the record, never through the manager
questions.explanation: The one channel.
